### **Overview**

This is an assignment to make a plot where at least one axis is a factor in a meaningful order, rather than R's default alphabetical order.

### **Load Libraries**

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)    #clean dataset
library(ggbeeswarm) #swarm plot 
library(calecopal)  #color palette of California
```

### **Load Data**

We are using intertidal data collected from 15 sites, 10 transects per site spanning from low to high intertidal zone, recording percent cover of bare rock, algae, mussels, anemone, and several categories of barnacles, and actual counts of whelks, crabs, and stars.

```{r}
intertidal <- read_csv(here("Week_09", "Data", "intertidaldata.csv"))
latitude <- read_csv(here("Week_09", "Data", "intertidaldata_latitude.csv"))
```

### **Clean and Prep Data**

I first joined both data set by `Site`. Then I cleaned column names and the `Quadrat` column with the `{janitor}` package. The raw column names had spaces and parentheses, so I converted these to consistent snake_case format. The `Quadrat` column had entries with trailing numbers or period, so I cleaned this up to ensure there are only 3 unique entries for this column.

```{r}
full_data <- intertidal |> 
  left_join(latitude, by = "Site") |> #Join both datasets by Site
  clean_names() |>                    #Convert column names to consistent snake_case format  
  mutate(quadrat = str_remove(quadrat, "[.0-9]+$"), #Remove trailing periods and numbers at the very end of the string
         quadrat = str_squish(quadrat))             #Remove all excess whitespace

names(intertidal) #Check column names before cleaning
names(full_data)  #Check column names after cleaning

sort(unique(intertidal$Quadrat)) #Check unique entries for Quadrat before cleaning
sort(unique(full_data$quadrat))  #Check unique entries for quadrat after cleaning
```

### **Figure 1: Plot visualizing by tide height, in order from Low to High**

Here I plotted algae percent cover by tide height. The `quadrat` column was converted into a factor and manually ordered since the order isn't determined by any data.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tide-height-plot
#| fig-cap: "Algae percent cover by tide height from low to high."
#| fig-align: "center" #center aligns the figure

full_data |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(quadrat, levels = c("Low", "Mid", "High")), #Convert into a factor and ordered manually
             y = algae,
             color = quadrat)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "white") +
  geom_beeswarm(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA) +
  guides (color = "none") +
  labs(title = "Algae Dominate Low Intertidal Zone",
       x = "Tide Height",
       y = "Algae Cover (%)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cal_palette("superbloom3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10))
  
```

### **Figure 2: Plot visualizing by site, in order of latitude**

Here I plotted algae percent cover by site. The `site` column was converted into a factor and ordered by the `latitude` column in descending order so it goes from North to South.

```{r}
#| label: fig-site-latitude-plot
#| fig-cap: "Low intertidal algae percent cover across sites from North to South."
#| fig-align: "center" #center aligns the figure

full_data |> 
  filter(quadrat == "Low") |> #Filter for only low intertidal data
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(site, latitude, .desc = TRUE), #Convert site into a factor and ordered by latitude
             y = algae,
             color = site)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_beeswarm() +
  guides (color = "none") +
  labs(title = "Low Intertidal Algae Cover Across Sites",
       x = "Site (North → South)",
       y = "Low Intertidal Algae Cover (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) #Angle text and aligned last letter to tick marks
```
